full_judgment:
Khademul Islam Chowdhury J: This appeal at the instance of the claimant of the goods, Md Sharif Khan is directed against an order being order No.40 dated 17-11-2003 passed by the learned Sessions Judge and the Special Tribunal, Chapai Nawabgonj in Special Tribunal Case No.103/2002 arising out of Shibganj PS Case No. 40 dated 16-7-2002 under section 25B of the Special Powers Act corresponding to GR Case No. 226 of 2002. 

 4. The facts material for disposal of this appeal, in short, is that the appellant imported 9,37,467 square feet marble tile from India and when the goods arrived at Sona Masjid Customs Office, C&F agent of the appellant paid usual customs duty and other taxes, obtained release and kept the goods in his godown. On 25-7-2002, 1728 pieces (3456 square feet) marble tiles were loaded in a Rajshahi-bound truck for transportation. On 26-7-2002 one JCO of the BDR, Bidyut Mitra detained the marble tiles on board and deposited the same with customs office at Nawabgonj and a complaint was lodged for alleged smuggling of the goods leading to Shibganj PS Case No. 40 dated 26-7-2002 under section 25B of the Special Powers Act. 

 8. On consideration of the order dated 19-11-2002 it appears that the learned Special Tribunal and the Sessions Judge, Chapai Nawabgonj disposed of the Special Tribunal Case No.103 of 2002, discharged the only accused in the case who was the truck driver and not the owner of the goods, and by the same order directed for return of the goods to the appellant on an application under section 517(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure with the finding that those goods were duly imported by the appellant and not smuggled into Bangladesh. But the same goods are also liable for detention and confiscation if they are imported into or exported from Bangladesh evading payment of leviable customs duties or in violation of any prohibition or restriction on the importation or accordingly, in breach of sections 15 and 16 of the Customs Act, 1969. 

 9. It is admitted in the petition of appeal that the learned Special Tribunal Judge directed the Customs Authority to submit detailed report about the seized marble tiles in connection with the hearing of application for return of sale proceed filed by the appellant in this case. Accordingly, the Customs Authority submitted report before the Tribunal vide Nathi No. 5(cus) 19/LC /Pita/Nawab/2002/ 567 dated 2-8-2003. The learned Tribunal Judge on scrutiny of the report rejected the prayer of the appellant for return of the sale proceeds upon holding that the goods had been confiscated by the Customs Authority.
